headline: Haverford outscores every Centennial rival
dek: Haverford scored 45 goals across all matches while allowing only thirteen, pairing that output with fifteen wins, two draws, and four losses. Even with the conference's highest overall goal total, Haverford finished behind Johns Hopkins and Dickinson in the Centennial table.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Scoring separates sharply at the extremes of the Centennial: Haverford's 45 goals surpass Washington College and Franklin & Marshall combined, leaving the lowest-scoring programs well behind a tightly bunched middle.

wire.line: Johns Hopkins finished with fourteen wins, two draws, and five losses overall while topping the Centennial table.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: McDaniel finished with nine wins, two draws, and eight losses overall, scoring 33 goals and allowing 30 despite sitting bottom of the conference table.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Washington College drew six matches, more than any other Centennial program, as part of a season with three wins and seven losses.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Swarthmore spread its attack across at least fifteen different goal scorers.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Ursinus goalkeeper Josiah Moore recorded 66 saves and six shutouts while conceding eighteen goals.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Five scheduled matches have passed their dates with no published result, including Dickinson's trip to Lebanon Valley and Muhlenberg's visit to Rutgers-Camden.

last_match.line: The defeat ended a winning run for the Centennial table leader, which had beaten Haverford and Roger Williams in its prior outings.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
